paragraphs: Here's what I think the Big Idea is, friend. God doesn't just look at what we DO for Him, but at WHY we do it. He asks the people, "was it really for Me that you fasted?" (Zechariah 7:5). That question lands right where it hurts, because you can do a religious thing for years and never once check who it's for.

And God doesn't leave them guessing about what He wants. He says, "Administer true justice. Show loving devotion and compassion to one another." (Zechariah 7:9). He names the widow, the fatherless, the foreigner and the poor, and says do not oppress them (Zechariah 7:10). So a heart that's really turned toward God shows up in how it treats the people right in front of it.

The sad part is that they heard all of it and still "stopped up their ears from hearing" (Zechariah 7:11). Hardened hearts do real damage, and I'd say that's a heavy part of this passage, but the good news for you and me is that God still speaks and still asks. So today, baker, let Him ask you the question, and let your answer show up in how you love the people around you. The story isn't over, because Bethel's question about fasting is still sitting on the table.
